title: Nehemiah 11:25–36
context: The towns and villages outside Jerusalem where the people of Judah and Benjamin settled, from Beersheba to the valley of Hinnom and from Geba westward to Lod and Ono, with a note that some Levitical divisions from Judah settled in Benjamin. Many of these sites cannot be located with certainty.

verses.text: As for the villages with their fields, some of the children of Judah lived in Kiriath Arba and its towns, in Dibon and its towns, in Jekabzeel and its villages,
verses.arminianNotes: Some of Judah live in Kiriath Arba, Dibon, and Jekabzeel with their towns. Arminian readers see the people resettling places with deep roots in Israel’s history.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the land reoccupied after exile. Kiriath Arba is the older name for Hebron in Joshua 14:15, though readers in this tradition hold other site identifications cautiously.

verses.text: in Jeshua, in Moladah, Beth Pelet,
verses.arminianNotes: They live in Jeshua, Moladah, and Beth Pelet. Arminian readers see the southern towns of Judah repopulated, extending the community beyond Jerusalem.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the resettlement of Judah’s territory. The precise locations of several of these towns are uncertain, and readers in this tradition hold identifications loosely.

verses.text: in Hazar Shual, in Beersheba and its towns,
verses.arminianNotes: They live in Hazar Shual and Beersheba with its towns. Arminian readers see the far south of Judah reoccupied, reaching toward the traditional boundary of the land.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the resettlement extending to Beersheba. The list recalls the allotments of Joshua 15, though the post-exilic settlement is described on its own terms.

verses.text: in Ziklag, in Meconah and in its towns,
verses.arminianNotes: They live in Ziklag and Meconah with its towns. Arminian readers see places with earlier histories, such as Ziklag in David’s story, inhabited again.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see continuity with Israel’s past. The location of Meconah is uncertain, and readers in this tradition do not press an identification.

verses.text: in En Rimmon, in Zorah, in Jarmuth,
verses.arminianNotes: They live in En Rimmon, Zorah, and Jarmuth. Arminian readers see the community reclaiming towns in the lowland and hill country of Judah.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the land resettled. The list records names without describing the size or condition of these communities.

verses.text: Zanoah, Adullam, and their villages, Lachish and its fields, and Azekah and its towns. So they encamped from Beersheba to the valley of Hinnom.
verses.arminianNotes: They live in Zanoah, Adullam, Lachish, and Azekah, so they “encamped from Beersheba to the valley of Hinnom.” Arminian readers see the extent of Judah’s settlement summarized.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the boundaries of the resettlement marked. The word “encamped” may suggest a modest or provisional settlement, though readers in this tradition do not press the term.

verses.text: The children of Benjamin also lived from Geba onward, at Michmash and Aija, and at Bethel and its towns,
verses.arminianNotes: The children of Benjamin live from Geba onward, at Michmash, Aija, and Bethel. Arminian readers see Benjamin’s territory reoccupied alongside Judah’s.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the resettlement of Benjamin. Bethel, once a center of false worship, is now listed among the towns of the restored community.

verses.arminianNotes: They live at Anathoth, Nob, and Ananiah. Arminian readers see towns with priestly and prophetic associations inhabited again.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see continuity with earlier history, as Anathoth was Jeremiah’s hometown in Jeremiah 1:1. The location of Ananiah is uncertain.

verses.arminianNotes: They live at Hazor, Ramah, and Gittaim. Arminian readers see further Benjamite towns resettled, strengthening the community around Jerusalem.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the land reoccupied. This Hazor is generally distinguished from the northern city of that name, though its exact site is uncertain.

verses.arminianNotes: They live at Hadid, Zeboim, and Neballat. Arminian readers see the community spreading into the western reaches of Benjamin’s territory.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the resettlement continuing. The locations of these towns are not certain, and readers in this tradition hold identifications cautiously.

verses.text: Lod, and Ono, the valley of craftsmen.
verses.arminianNotes: They live at Lod and Ono, “the valley of craftsmen.” Arminian readers see towns known for skilled work inhabited by the restored community.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the list reaching its western edge. Ono appears in Nehemiah 6:2 as the place where Nehemiah’s enemies sought to meet him.

verses.text: Of the Levites, certain divisions in Judah settled in Benjamin’s territory.
verses.arminianNotes: “Of the Levites, certain divisions in Judah settled in Benjamin’s territory.” Arminian readers see the Levites distributed among the tribes for service.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the Levites placed throughout the land. The closing note reflects the pattern of Levites living among the tribes rather than in a single territory.
